title: Critical Care Nurses
description: Provide specialized nursing care for patients in critical or coronary care units.

tasks.text: Monitor patients for changes in status and indications of conditions such as sepsis or shock and institute appropriate interventions.
Monitor patients' fluid intake and output to detect emerging problems, such as fluid and electrolyte imbalances.
Conduct pulmonary assessments to identify abnormal respiratory patterns or breathing sounds that indicate problems.
Assess patients' pain levels or sedation requirements.
Administer blood and blood products, monitoring patients for signs and symptoms related to transfusion reactions.
Identify malfunctioning equipment or devices.
Identify patients at risk of complications due to nutritional status.
Provide post-mortem care.
Ensure that equipment or devices are properly stored after use.
Evaluate patients' vital signs or laboratory data to determine emergency intervention needs.
Prioritize nursing care for assigned critically ill patients, based on assessment data or identified needs.
Compile and analyze data obtained from monitoring or diagnostic tests.
Assess family adaptation levels and coping skills to determine whether intervention is needed.
Assess patients' psychosocial status and needs, including areas such as sleep patterns, anxiety, grief, anger, and support systems.
Identify patients' age-specific needs and alter care plans as necessary to meet those needs.
Participate in professional organizations and continuing education to improve practice knowledge and skills.
Document patients' medical histories and assessment findings.
Collect specimens for laboratory tests.
Set up and monitor medical equipment and devices such as cardiac monitors, mechanical ventilators and alarms, oxygen delivery devices, transducers, or pressure lines.
Perform approved therapeutic or diagnostic procedures, based upon patients' clinical status.
Document patients' treatment plans, interventions, outcomes, or plan revisions.
Participate in the development, review, or evaluation of nursing practice protocols.
Administer medications intravenously, by injection, orally, through gastric tubes, or by other methods.
Collaborate with other health care professionals to develop and revise treatment plans, based on identified needs and assessment data.
Advocate for patients' and families' needs, or provide emotional support for patients and their families.
Assist physicians with procedures such as bronchoscopy, endoscopy, endotracheal intubation, or elective cardioversion.
Supervise and monitor unit nursing staff.
Coordinate patient care conferences.
Plan, provide, or evaluate educational programs for nursing staff, interdisciplinary health care team members, or community members.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Medical software
skills.def: Software to evaluate, plan, or redesign healthcare procedures. May include reporting or visualization features. Examples: Allscripts Professional EHR, Amkai AmkaiCharts, Bizmatics PrognoCIS EMR, Cerner Millennium.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Microsoft SharePoint.

skills.name: Information retrieval or search software
skills.def: Software to efficiently search or access data from sources such as large collections of documents. Examples: American Association of Critical Care Nurses AACN Medicopeia, PEPID RN Critical Care RNCC.

skills.name: Cloud-based data access and sharing software
skills.def: Software to share or co-author computer files through cloud computing, where documents are stored in a central "cloud" of networked servers. Examples: Google Drive.

skills.name: Human resources software
skills.def: Software to manage employee evaluations, track wages or absenteeism, maintain safety records, or manage hours or time off. Examples: Oracle Taleo.
